description: We are the Earthbound Explorers, finding places on Earth that match the Moon and Mars.
summary: GeoProxy is an interactive planetary-analog discovery tool for future Moon and Mars exploration. Rather than relying on a fixed list of famous terrestrial analog sites, it searches global Earth terrain data to identify locations that best match selected planetary targets. Users can explore linked 3D globes of Earth, Mars, and the Moon; select sites such as Jezero Crater or Shackleton Crater; and inspect ranked Earth candidates. GeoProxy compares shared 20 km terrain features—relief, median slope, and surface roughness—across 318,539 valid Earth land windows. It also provides NASA imagery, land-cover and geological context, source provenance, and an “Illusion Break” panel that clearly explains where an Earth analogy fails, including atmosphere, radiation, gravity, and temperature differences. GeoProxy turns open planetary and Earth-observation data into a transparent tool for discovering and characterizing potential field-test locations.
details:
GeoProxy helps researchers, educators, and exploration planners move from “Which famous Earth analogue should we use?” to “Which locations best match the physical conditions of this specific Moon or Mars target?”

The user begins by choosing a planetary target, such as Jezero Crater on Mars, Shackleton Crater near the lunar south pole, Gale Crater, Elysium Planitia, or the Apollo 11 region. GeoProxy displays the target on an interactive globe and compares its terrain with a global Earth search.

Our matching pipeline measures three transferable terrain features over a common 20 km window:

  • Relief: the 90th–10th percentile elevation range
  • Median slope: typical surface steepness
  • Terrain roughness: average local elevation variation

We first screen 1,268,157 Earth windows and retain 318,539 valid land windows, excluding ocean-dominated and heavily glaciated locations. We then confirm leading candidates at a finer resolution. Features are log-transformed and scaled by Earth-wide variability; the resulting ranking shows the closest matches under equal weights and can be explored with feature-weight controls.

GeoProxy does not present its score as a probability or proof that two sites are equivalent. The score is a relative terrain-similarity ranking within the selected datasets and model. Each candidate includes an evidence panel showing feature-by-feature agreement, land cover, geological context, climate context, provenance, and an explicit “Illusion Break.” This section identifies important non-analogous conditions such as vacuum, radiation exposure, gravity, atmospheric pressure, and differences in temperature measurement.

For Jezero Crater, GeoProxy’s top candidate is near Waxxari, Xinjiang, China. Its 20 km terrain window closely matches Jezero in relief, slope, and roughness, and has 89% bare or sparse ground. However, its geology is only a partial match and its terrestrial atmosphere and climate are not Mars-like—an example of why transparent limits are central to GeoProxy.

The prototype is built as a lightweight web application with HTML, JavaScript, CSS, Node.js, and Python geospatial preprocessing. The interface uses interactive globe visualizations, reproducible precomputed rankings, map-linked evidence cards, and NASA imagery for visual context.

Our next step is to add physically justified environmental variables only where measurements can be compared across worlds, expand the target catalogue, improve geological sampling from point lookups to spatial proportions, and support higher-resolution local field-planning analyses.
dataRefs: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) / Landsat WELD imagery
